protocol.name: helix_screenshot_v1

description.summary: screen captures for the Helix shell

protocol.description: A private protocol between the Helix compositor and the Helix shell. The shell serves org.gnome.Shell.Screenshot on D-Bus; in GNOME the shell and the compositor are one process, in Helix they are separate, so the shell asks the compositor for the pixels with this protocol. The global is only advertised to privileged clients (the shell the compositor launched itself).

interface.name: helix_screenshot_manager_v1
interface.description: Each request captures the scene as it is when the compositor handles the request, so surfaces the shell destroyed before sending it are not in the image. The compositor writes a PNG image to the given file descriptor (from its current offset) and closes its copy, then sends done or failed on the new object. Coordinates are logical layout pixels; the image has as many pixels per logical pixel as the highest scale among the monitors it covers.

entry.name: hidden
entry.summary: leave the pointer out

entry.name: shown
entry.summary: draw the pointer when it is inside

request.name: capture_screen
request.description: One image covering the bounding box of the layout; parts no monitor shows are transparent.

request.name: capture_area

description.summary: capture a rectangle of the layout

request.description: Width and height must be positive.

request.name: capture_window
request.description: The window's surfaces, cropped to its window geometry.

request.name: capture_window_with_frame

description.summary: capture the focused window and its title bar

request.description: As capture_window, but with the title bar the compositor draws above X11 windows (if any) included at the top.

request.name: capture_window_at

description.summary: capture the window at a point, with its title bar

request.description: As capture_window_with_frame, for the window shown at x, y (layout coordinates) instead of the focused one; failed with no_window when there is none.

request.name: capture_window_id

description.summary: capture a window by its window list id

request.description: The surfaces of window (its id in helix_window_list_v1), cropped to its window geometry, whether or not it is shown (on another workspace, minimized); no title bar or cursor. Drawn at the primary monitor's scale. Failed with no_window for an unknown window.

request.name: copy_image

description.summary: put a PNG image on the clipboard

request.description: The compositor reads a PNG image from the file descriptor (from its current offset to the end), takes the clipboard selection and offers the image as image/png to Wayland and X11 clients until something else takes the selection.

request.name: copy_text
request.description: The compositor reads UTF-8 text from the file descriptor (from its current offset to the end), takes the clipboard selection and offers the text as text/plain;charset=utf-8, text/plain, UTF8_STRING, STRING and TEXT to Wayland and X11 clients until something else takes the selection.

request.name: copy_data

description.summary: put an agent's data on the clipboard

request.description: For Agent Access: the compositor reads data from the file descriptor (from its current offset to the end), takes the clipboard selection and offers it as mime_type until something else takes the selection. text/plain;charset=utf-8 and text/plain (UTF-8 text) are offered as copy_text offers text. Its source reads as agent in helix_clipboard_info_v1.

request.name: get_clipboard

description.summary: what the clipboard offers, and who set it

request.description: The new object receives an offer event for each type the clipboard selection offers (none when there is none), then done.

request.name: receive_clipboard
request.description: Has the clipboard selection's owner write it, as mime_type, into the file descriptor, and closes the compositor's copy. Only while the selection is still the one generation (from helix_clipboard_info_v1.done) names and it offers mime_type: otherwise the descriptor is closed with nothing written.

request.name: agent_capture
request.description:
For Agent Access's Screenshot method: an image of the layout rectangle x, y, width, height (window 0), or of window (its window list id; drawn whether or not it is shown, cropped to its window geometry, and then to x, y, width, height in the window when width is positive), never with the pointer.
Everything the shell has not cleared is drawn as opaque black in its place in the stacking order (what is above it is drawn over it), so a window or surface that appears after the shell decided is never shown: in a layout capture, every window whose window list id is not in shown (an array of uint32, in host byte order; its rectangle with its popups and title bar), every window that has none (X11 override-redirect windows), and every layer surface whose namespace is not one of layers (comma-separated; its rectangle with its popups). Layer surfaces hidden by a full-screen window are not drawn and not filled. The frame's filled event says how many were filled in the rectangle captured, before done. Failed with locked while the session is locked, no_window for a window that is unknown or not in shown, and invalid for an empty rectangle, one outside the layout or window, or an image of more than 8192 pixels either way.

request.name: agent_input
request.description: For Agent Access's Input method: a run of synthetic input into window (its window list id). See helix_agent_input_v1.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Captures in progress are not affected.

interface.name: helix_screenshot_frame_v1
interface.description: Receives exactly one done or failed event.

entry.name: locked
entry.summary: the session is locked

entry.name: no_window
entry.summary: no window has focus

entry.name: invalid
entry.summary: empty area or nothing to capture

entry.name: failed
entry.summary: rendering or writing the image failed

event.name: done
event.description: The rectangle captured, in logical layout coordinates.

event.name: filled
event.description: agent_capture only, before done: how many windows and surfaces were filled in the rectangle captured.

interface.name: helix_clipboard_info_v1
interface.description: Receives offer events and then exactly one done event; the shell destroys it after done.

entry.name: none
entry.summary: no selection

entry.name: app
entry.summary: a Wayland client (app_id and pid say which)

entry.name: x11
entry.summary: an X11 app (app_id and pid: the focused X11 window's, when it took the selection)

entry.name: shell
entry.summary: the shell (its text fields, copy_image, copy_text)

entry.name: remote
entry.summary: a remote desktop session's client

event.name: done
event.description: generation changes whenever the selection does; app_id is the app id of a window of the client that set it ("" when unknown), pid its process (0 when unknown).

interface.name: helix_agent_input_v1

description.summary: an agent's synthetic input into one window

interface.description:
Requests are carried out in order, one at a time; each is answered with done once carried out, or the run ends with stopped (and nothing more is carried out). Positions are logical pixels in the window's geometry (its top-left corner is 0, 0).
Before every key, button, motion and scroll event the compositor checks that the session is not locked, no Agent Access prompt is shown, the window is still mapped and has the keyboard focus (also through one of its popups), for keys and text that the app's focused text field (zwp_text_input_v3) is not a password or PIN field, and, for pointer events, that the point is inside the window and the surface there is the window's own (not another window, a title bar or a shell surface over it). Events go straight to the client: never through the compositor's key bindings, the shell's keys, click-to-focus or window moving.
Input from anything else (the machine's devices, a remote desktop session, EIS, the headless test socket: a key or button press, pointer motion, scrolling, a touch) stops the run at once (stopped user_input) and refuses new runs for a while (stopped cooldown). Keys and buttons the run holds are released when it ends.

entry.name: cancelled
entry.summary: cancel was sent

entry.name: user_input
entry.summary: the user used an input device

entry.name: cooldown
entry.summary: the user used an input device moments ago

entry.name: locked
entry.summary: the session is locked

entry.name: prompt
entry.summary: an Agent Access prompt is shown

entry.name: gone
entry.summary: the window is gone or not mapped

entry.name: focus
entry.summary: the window does not have the keyboard focus

entry.name: outside
entry.summary: the point is outside the window or covered

entry.name: no_key
entry.summary: the keyboard layout has no key for a keysym

entry.name: invalid
entry.summary: a malformed request

entry.name: password
entry.summary: a key or text while the app's focused text field is a password or PIN field (its text-input-v3 content purpose)

description.summary: move the pointer to x, y in the window

request.name: button

description.summary: a pointer button down or up where the pointer is

request.description: button is an evdev code (272 left, 273 right, 274 middle).

request.name: scroll
request.description: By steps of a wheel (positive: right, down).

request.name: key

description.summary: a key of the user's layout down or up

request.description: The key that gives keysym in the active layout, at its first or second level (with Shift around it for the second); stopped no_key when there is none.

request.name: text
request.description: Each character as a key of a keymap made for the text, pressed and released with no modifiers, whatever the user's layout, Caps Lock or held keys (line feed is Return, tab is Tab).

request.name: cancel
request.description: Stops the run (stopped cancelled), even in the middle of a text.

description.summary: end the run, releasing what it holds
the oldest request not yet answered was carried out
the run ended; nothing more is carried out
